title: Bug: `rif_support` should be derived from interface chosen for testing `rif_rx_ifaces` rather arbritary interface `rif_iface`
author: Javier-Tan
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

Currently `ip/test_ip_packet.py` detects `rif_support` via checking if arbritarily chosen `rif_iface` `rx_err` field is N/A:
```
rif_counter_out = parse_rif_counters(
    duthost.command("show interfaces counters rif")["stdout_lines"])
rif_iface = list(rif_counter_out.keys())[0]
rif_support = False if rif_counter_out[rif_iface]['rx_err'] == 'N/A' else True
```

We have encountered situations where the first `iface` may indicate `rif_support = True`, but `rif_support` should be False, e.g.:
```
          IFACE    RX_OK    RX_BPS    RX_PPS    RX_ERR    TX_OK    TX_BPS    TX_PPS    TX_ERR
 --------------  -------  --------  --------  --------  -------  --------  --------  --------
  Ethernet-Rec0      N/A       N/A       N/A         0      N/A       N/A       N/A         0
 PortChannel101      N/A       N/A       N/A       N/A      N/A       N/A       N/A       N/A
 ...
```
Where `Ethernet-Rec0` is an inband port for VoQ, not a physical front-panel port. (Whether or not this is a bug or not is still under investigation).

When having `rif_support = True` when we are receiving `N/A` on ports means we error with failures e.g.: 
```
...
  File "/var/src/sonic-mgmt_vmstr-ut2-nh5010-5/tests/ip/test_ip_packet.py", line 165, in test_forward_ip_packet_with_0x0000_chksum
    rx_err = int(rif_counter_out[rif_rx_ifaces]["rx_err"].replace(",", "")) if rif_support else 0
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'N/A'
```

A more reliable way to determine if `rif_support` should be True or False, is simply by checking `rx_err` / `tx_err` of the chosen rif for testing, `rif_rx_ifaces`, rather than arbritarily checking `rif_iface = list(rif_counter_out.keys())[0]`

### Steps to Reproduce

Under investigation, has happened twice during testing on `NH5010-5` devices with URH min topology.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Check if `rif_support` is True or False, by checking if `rx_err`/`tx_err` = `N/A` on the actual iface being tested, `rif_rx_ifaces`. This will ensure that there aren't any failures like `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'N/A'`

### Relevant log output

```shell
See above
```

### Output of `show version`

```shell
20251110.29
```

### Attach files (if any)

N/A
